summary: Whatsmeow arm added additively; simulado default untouched; e2e test drives the real binary over a live IPC socket; contract-check 0 violations. Non-blocking notes recorded.
notes: contract-check ok=true, 0 violations; not_checked: forbid.behaviors. All 18 behavior clauses were verified by hand: the IPC protocol/backup docs, everything under sidecar/ (Go), the whole hexcell-canal-whatsmeow crate, motor.rs, hexcell-core/canal.rs, procesador.rs, inferencia.rs and salud.rs are untouched; no new dependency, no Docker or container tooling, no sleep-based test synchronization.

Default-path sanctity confirmed. main.rs is +30/-0, so the Simulado arm and every line before the channel match are byte-for-byte unchanged. tests/configuracion.rs is +44/-1 where the single deletion is only the `use` line gaining CanalSeleccionado; no existing test body was modified. falla_si_el_canal_no_es_reconocido and el_binario_no_vincula_nada_si_la_configuracion_es_invalida keep passing unmodified.

Fail-closed startup verified: Configuracion::desde_entorno runs before GestorDePools::abrir, AlmacenDeIdentidad::abrir and servir_salud, so an invalid HEXCELL_CANAL aborts before any port bind or store open. The Spanish ValorInvalido error names HEXCELL_CANAL and now lists 'uno de: simulado, whatsmeow'; the pre-existing test asserts the concrete variable name.

Test honesty (LES-033): canal_whatsmeow_seleccionado.rs drives the REAL compiled binary (CARGO_BIN_EXE_hexcell with env_clear) against a live Unix socket, performs a real version-4 saludo handshake, injects one evento_entrante and asserts an outbound mensaje_saliente carrying id_conversacion=conv-01 and marca_temporal_origen_ms=1700000000000. mensaje_saliente is emitted only through the adapter's ChannelAdapter::enviar, which only Motor calls after ProcesadorDeInferencia, so the asserted evidence does prove engine traversal; a stub or echo could only live inside the whatsmeow crate, which the contract forbids touching and the diff does not touch.

Test-strength gap (non-blocking): the e2e test does not assert the reply body against ProveedorSimulado's deterministic 'respuesta simulada {huella:016x}' (crates/hexcell/src/inferencia.rs:143), so a degraded or fallback reply would pass identically.

Ordering assumption (non-blocking, low flake risk): the e2e test asserts frame #1 is confirmacion and frame #2 is mensaje_saliente. The adapter confirms immediately after a non-blocking mpsc send (adaptador.rs:483) while the outbound needs dedup + repository + inference, so the order holds in practice (5/5 stability reps green), but it is not guaranteed by construction on the multi-thread runtime. Reading both frames order-agnostically would be strictly more robust.

AC-2's 'and the existing adapter identity store' clause rests on a wrong spec assumption: AdaptadorWhatsmeow::nuevo takes four positional args and no identity-store parameter, because the JID mapping for the real channel lives in the sidecar's own HEXCELL_RUTA_IDENTIDAD store. The blueprint documented this as an explicit risk and the contract forbids inventing the parameter; main.rs keeps opening AlmacenDeIdentidad unconditionally before the match. The implementation is compliant, not deficient.

adr-0010 clean: no phone number and no raw transport identifier appears in nucleo configuration, logs, scripts or STATUS prose. HEXCELL_TELEFONO_CELULA in scripts/laboratorio/entorno.ejemplo.sh is a real sidecar variable (sidecar/internal/configuracion/configuracion.go:34) read from the operator's own environment with an empty default and no literal, exactly what the contract requires. Hygiene nit: the shared env file is sourced by BOTH launchers, so the number also lands in the nucleo's process environment even though the nucleo never reads it; exporting it only from iniciar-sidecar.sh would be cleaner.

Lab scripts are functional, not decorative: every exported variable is really consumed (HEXCELL_RUTA_SQLSTORE, HEXCELL_RUTA_IDENTIDAD and HEXCELL_TELEFONO_CELULA by the Go config; HEXCELL_CANAL, HEXCELL_SOCKET_IPC, HEXCELL_RUTA_DATOS and HEXCELL_DIRECCION_SALUD by the Rust config), and 'go run .' resolves because sidecar/main.go is package main at the module root. Paths default under a configurable /tmp lab root, so there is no hardcoded user-absolute path. Spanish comments and the honest 'lab harness, A-6 owns the operable packaging' warning are present in all three files.

Doc-rot (minor, non-blocking): crates/hexcell/src/configuracion.rs still documents CANAL_POR_DEFECTO as 'el unico que existe hoy en el arbol', which is false now that Whatsmeow exists. The blueprint's step 2 asked for that stale claim to be retired; the enum doc comment was fixed but this const comment kept it.

Lab-session caveat for the human (pre-existing, out of this contract's reach): EstadoDeSalud is built with SesionDelCanal::siempre_activa() before the channel match, so /health/ready returns 200 on the whatsmeow arm regardless of real channel state. During the task-15 rehearsal (network cut, forced unlink) the health endpoint will NOT reflect the outage. AdaptadorWhatsmeow::suscribir_estado exists, but wiring it into health needs salud.rs, which this contract forbids.

docs/STATUS.md is a pure one-line append: a Definido entry dated 2026-08-18, traced to HEX-025 / task 15 of stage A-3 / FR-12, recording both human decisions (direct processes with the container-restart rehearsal explicitly re-run in A-6; ProveedorSimulado until A-4). No prior entry edited or deleted, absolute dates, no invented numbers, no mass-sending vocabulary introduced, and nothing implying Fase B replaces or retires the sidecar. AC-5's conditional clause does not trigger: no existing STATUS or runbook line claims the engine only runs on the simulated channel.
PAT-034 not applicable: the diff touches no adaptador flow (hexcell-canal-whatsmeow is untouched); changes are confined to crates/hexcell, scripts/laboratorio and docs/STATUS.md, as expected.

Duplication note (accepted): the Whatsmeow arm repeats the provider/procesador/Motor/select! construction of the Simulado arm. The contract mandated an additive second match arm instead of a shared helper, so this is contract-directed, not unrequested refactoring.
acceptance-coverage: status=pass, 6/6 acceptance criteria covered, zero gaps. 05-validation.json: 7/7 contract commands exit 0, overall_result=passed.
